name: H&R Block, Inc.

profile.description: H&R Block is the largest consumer tax services company in the U.S., serving clients through approximately 9,000 company-owned and franchise retail offices, DIY tax software, the Spruce mobile banking platform (nearing $1B in customer deposits), and AI Tax Assist powered by OpenAI. New CEO Curtis Campbell (former TaxAct CEO, Intuit veteran) took over January 1, 2026 with a vision to build a year-round financial platform.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): H&R Block delivered fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $2.40B (+5.3% YoY) and raised full-year guidance to revenue of $3.91-$3.92B and EBITDA of $1.025-$1.035B — CEO Campbell called the season 'an important inflection point' with improved assisted market share trends after years of pressure [1]. The OpenAI partnership and CEO transition from Jones to Campbell represent a significant strategic evolution. AI Deployment (2/2): AI Tax Assist (consumer) and Sidekick (professional) built with OpenAI are deployed at scale across millions of DIY users and 60,000+ tax professionals, representing material AI deployment with measurable client engagement [2]. Market Share (1/2): HRB stabilized its assisted channel market share after two years of improving trends — 'market share performance was favorable each week throughout the season' [1] — but is not gaining meaningful share against Intuit TurboTax in DIY. Pipeline (1/2): Block Horizons strategy aims to transform HRB into a year-round financial platform; Spruce banking (476K signups, nearing $1B deposits) is gaining traction, but specific revenue targets and timelines for the broader platform vision remain undisclosed [2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Material investment in AI (OpenAI partnership), Wave small-business software, and DIY platform improvements at levels appropriate for the company's scale.

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): H&R Block's purpose centers on 'providing help and inspiring confidence in our clients and communities everywhere' — clear about what the company does and for whom, and connected to the co-founders' legacy of service, but not deeply distinctive or validated by transformative execution beyond the tax category [4]. Community Impact (1/2): 'Make Every Block Better' community impact platform, honoring co-founders Henry and Richard Bloch's legacy of service, 'Path to Print Less' initiative reduced printed pages 36%, and associate-led composting program at headquarters [3]. These are genuine but modest community investments. Employee Retention (1/2): CEO transition from Jeff Jones (8-year modernizer) to Curtis Campbell was managed smoothly with Jones remaining as strategic advisor through September 2026 [2]. Campbell's track record at TaxAct and Intuit brings credibility, though seasonal preparer turnover remains structurally high. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider buying by executives. Aggressive share buybacks are corporate capital allocation, not personal conviction purchases.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as Dividend stock. FY2026 full-year guidance raised to revenue of $3.91-$3.92B (+4.1% YoY) and EBITDA of $1.025-$1.035B (+5.5% YoY), with adjusted EPS of $5.10-$5.20 (+10.5% YoY) [1]. Forward P/E of 5.92 is exceptionally low, well within the 20 target — the standout metric in this profile. Profit margin of 18.9% is near the 20% target. ROE of 673% is artificially inflated by buyback-depleted equity base but scores at the 1.0 cap. D/E is extremely high (>>300%) due to years of aggressive share repurchases reducing book equity to near-zero — this scores 0 mechanically but reflects capital return strategy, not financial distress [5]. Dividend metrics are strong: 39+ years of payments, 11 consecutive years of growth, payout ratio of ~29.6%, and yield of 4.64%. Revenue growth 5yr CAGR of -2.1% is the key weakness, reflecting secular pressure on the tax preparation industry before the recent inflection [1].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (4/9): Tax preparation is squarely in AI's displacement crosshairs — AI can materially improve DIY tax outcomes and reduce demand for assisted human preparation over time [2]. The core assisted business (~60% of revenue) faces real substitution risk as AI assistants become capable of handling increasingly complex tax situations. However, H&R Block has near-term durability through its 9,000-office physical footprint, fiduciary liability protections, and the regulatory complexity of the U.S. tax code. Campbell's 'year-round financial platform' strategy attempts to reposition beyond seasonal tax exposure. The company is deploying AI offensively (AI Tax Assist, Sidekick) rather than being passively disrupted, but the long-term outcome remains genuinely uncertain. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI Tax Assist and Sidekick powered by OpenAI are deployed at scale, materially integrated into premium products across 60,000 tax professionals, and driving measurable engagement improvements during the 2026 tax season [2].

infinite_game.summary: Under Jones and now Campbell, H&R Block is attempting to reinvent itself from a seasonal tax preparer into a year-round AI-powered financial platform. The Just Cause is evolving credibly through the OpenAI partnership and Spruce banking expansion, and leadership has shown courage to invest in transformation despite facing existential AI disruption risk. However, the company remains fundamentally dependent on the seasonal tax cycle, and the transformation's success is far from assured.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Campbell's vision of a 'year-round financial platform powered by software, data, and AI while preserving human trust' evolves the Bloch founding mission credibly [2]. Strategic decisions — the OpenAI partnership, Spruce banking launch, AI Tax Assist deployment — trace back to this purpose. The mission connects tax preparation to broader financial empowerment, though it hasn't yet been validated through a multi-decade track record of consistent execution.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO transition from Jones to Campbell was managed smoothly with a strategic advisor transition period through September 2026, demonstrating organizational maturity [2]. However, the seasonal tax preparer model is structurally high-turnover, and compensation ratings at 3.1/5 on Glassdoor indicate room for improvement in how frontline associates experience the organization.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): H&R Block competes primarily against Intuit TurboTax, but management language frames competition more in terms of market defense ('stabilized assisted market share') than learning from rivals' strengths [1]. Campbell's prior experience at Intuit provides personal awareness of the rival, but the company's public competitive stance is not explicitly infinite-minded.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Evolution from pure retail tax preparation to an omnichannel model (DIY + assisted + AI Tax Assist + Spruce banking + Wave small-business) represents real strategic diversification [2]. The OpenAI partnership is a meaningful capability pivot. However, the core 9,000-office retail footprint remains the backbone of the business — the transformation is incremental rather than a wholesale business model reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Jones invested in the OpenAI partnership and AI Tax Assist deployment during a period when AI posed existential risk to the core business — choosing to embrace the technology rather than resist it [2]. Aggressive buybacks paired with dividend discipline reflect conviction in long-term value. However, these bets are being made from a position of strong cash flow ($1B+ EBITDA) rather than genuine sacrifice.

investment_thesis: H&R Block delivered fiscal Q3 2026 revenue of $2.40B (+5.3% YoY) and raised full-year guidance to $3.91-$3.92B revenue and EBITDA of $1.025-$1.035B, with CEO Campbell declaring the season 'an important inflection point' as assisted market share trends turned favorable for the first time in years [1]. At forward P/E of 5.92 with a 4.64% dividend yield, 39-year payment history, 29.6% payout ratio, and $1B+ EBITDA, HRB offers compelling value for income-oriented investors. The OpenAI partnership positions H&R Block offensively against AI disruption rather than as a passive victim, with AI Tax Assist and Sidekick deployed at scale across 60,000 tax pros [2]. Campbell's vision to build a year-round financial platform — anchored by Spruce banking (nearing $1B in deposits) and Wave small-business software — provides optionality beyond the seasonal tax cycle.
thesis_continued: The bear case is secular AI substitution and growth limitations. As AI tax preparation tools become more capable, the pricing power and volume of the 9,000-office assisted channel could erode — this is the core revenue engine and the most vulnerable to AI displacement [2]. Revenue growth 5yr CAGR of -2.1% reflects structural pressure on the industry, and even with the Q3 inflection, full-year growth of ~4% is modest. IRS Direct File expansion and Intuit TurboTax competitive pressure add to the top-line risk. D/E of 1,750% (from buyback-depleted equity) is optically extreme though supported by $1B+ EBITDA. The Inspire Impact Score of -49 (MISALIGNED) reflecting LGBT activism may limit the faith-aligned investor base. Seasonality remains extreme — the business is fundamentally dependent on Q3/Q4 fiscal tax season, limiting visibility and creating binary risk around each tax filing period.
key_catalysts: OpenAI-powered AI Tax Assist and Sidekick deployed at scale, potentially increasing net average charge and client retention across 60,000 tax professionals and millions of DIY users [2]
Campbell's year-round financial platform strategy — Spruce banking nearing $1B deposits and Wave small-business software could unlock non-seasonal revenue streams [2]
Forward P/E of 5.92 and 4.64% dividend yield with 29.6% payout ratio provide significant margin of safety and capital return capacity via continued buybacks [5]
key_risks: AI-driven displacement of assisted tax preparation — as AI DIY tools become capable of handling complex returns, the premium pricing power of the 9,000-office channel erodes [2]
Revenue growth 5yr CAGR of -2.1% reflects structural industry decline; IRS Direct File expansion and Intuit TurboTax competitive pressure compound the top-line risk [1]
Extreme seasonality — business fundamentally dependent on Q3/Q4 fiscal tax season, with off-season quarters running at a loss, creating binary risk around each filing period [1]
